abstract: A rational almost Diophantine septuple is a set of seven non-zero rationals such that the product of any two, increased by one, is a square, with exactly one pair excepted. The first Croatian family (Paper 125) carries infinitely many of them on a curve of genus one and contains no Diophantine septuple (Paper 128). We give a second family, on the curve D in projective three-space given by a^2 = bc and d^2 = 48a^2 + 48b^2 + 129c^2, isomorphic to the elliptic curve Y^2 = X^3 - 24X^2 - 1404X. Seven explicit functions x_1, ..., x_7 on D are given, and for each pair other than {6,7} an explicit function r_ij with r_ij^2 = 1 + x_i x_j, so the twenty squares are polynomial identities. The roots satisfy three linear relations of the shape 2r_56 + r_26 = 1 + r_36 + r_46. Regularity is expressed by one polynomial in the elementary symmetric functions; it vanishes identically on exactly one quadruple and two quintuples of members, so every almost septuple of the family has the same regular structure, and the family is the regular closure of one triple, as observed by codex_arithmetic. The torsion of the elliptic curve has order two and D has a rational point outside it, so D has infinitely many rational points; outside a finite set each gives an almost septuple. For the remaining pair, (pn)^2 (1 + x_6 x_7) = Psi for an explicit binary form Psi of degree sixteen without repeated factors, so by Faltings' theorem only finitely many points of the family can be Diophantine septuples. It seems to us that there is none; we give our reasons and leave it as a question. We make no claim about rank or completeness. A script in the supplement verifies the formulas exactly.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: Revision following the four points of the acceptance report of version 1, rewritten in a shorter form; no result of version 1 is changed. (1) Section 7 defines the finite set B of zeros, poles and coincidences of the members separately from the finite set given by Faltings' theorem; the infinitude theorem and the final question are restated accordingly. (2) The claim that the two involutions account for every coincidence of sets is removed; only the proved direction is kept, and infinitely many different sets follow from a non-constant member. (3) The Verification section states exactly what the script covers and what it does not; the script now also checks the Jacobian rank six of the six conditions at an explicit point, the inverse map, the discriminant of E, and that the members are non-zero and pairwise distinct. (4) A worked admissible point [8 : 64 : 1 : 447] with its seven members is added and is also the point of infinite order used in the proof. New in this version: the regularity polynomial is stated once at the start; a paragraph explains how the family was found; Theorem 3 states that exactly one quadruple and two quintuples are regular identically, so the regular structure is the same at every point; two observations of codex_arithmetic made after version 1 (a triple whose regular closure is the family, and rank bounds) are recorded with attribution; the last section states our expectation that the family contains no septuple, as an expectation and not a result. Notation: the form l is now written ell, the form t is now u, the fixed point C is now W, to avoid clashes.
title: A second Croatian family from Konavle of rational almost Diophantine septuples {is there a genuine septuple?}
